title: Land model: stepped lids churn a retract-and-plunge at every lid step edge

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
## The churn, root-caused

Follow-up to #1286 (the land model), picking up the finding from my review of that PR: on a part whose surface is not flat, the path fragments around the lids — every crossing of a filled hole costs a retract → rapid → plunge every ~0.5–1 mm instead of one continuous lateral bridge.

The cause is downstream of the fill rule itself: **the closing levels a lid's cells a hair apart, and `emit` gives each cell its own height, so the lid is a staircase.** At each step edge the ball can seat on neither plane for a full ball-width annulus — the higher lid top blocks it from seating on the lower, and a lid top's free edge carries no fold support (lids are horizontal tops-only quads). Support goes `None` across that annulus, and the march retracts and plunges at every step.

Repro: the #1196 part (4B52391, two stepped through-holes, roof descending ~0.04 mm per 1.06 mm grid cell across hole 1). `fill_openings(width = 12.7, tol = 0.01)`, then `parallel` with `stepover 0.6`, ball Ø6, `tol 0.05`, `clearance_z 30`. Vertical feed moves near the hole centers:

| | fill off | fill on (current) | fill on (fixed) |
|---|---|---|---|
| near the holes | 22 | 166 | 40 |
| elsewhere | 36 | 128 | 57 |

(The `fill off` path is byte-identical baseline; the fix cuts the lid-induced plunges by ~75%.)

## The fix

One plane per opening: before emitting, lift the whole lid — the raised component **and** its one-cell ring — to the highest closed height over all of those cells (`Grid::plateau` in `fill.rs`). The plateau runs *after* the `enclosed` check, so enclosure is still judged against the closing's own levels. Doc-law updated: "One plane per opening" now covers the ring cells.

Regression test: `a_pocket_under_a_descending_roof_gets_one_flat_lid` in `crates/motion/tests/finish3d_land.rs` — a pocket under a shallow descending roof must come out coplanar, and the land never descends into the pocket.

## Bounded residuals (documented, not solved here)

Two narrow `None` zones remain at the lid/model boundary on the repro part, both inherent to tops-only lids:

- west rim: x ∈ [25.17, 25.40], **0.23 mm** — free-edge seating artifact where the lid is flush with the roof (7.085 vs 7.0848);
- east rim: x ∈ [31.76, 33.23], **1.47 mm** — the roof descends eastward (~0.27 mm drop to the ring's last cell), and a flat lid over a sloping roof always steps down to the real surface at its edge.

Both are ball-seating artifacts at the step, not interior churn. A follow-up giving lids side faces (or edge support at lid boundaries) could close them; I'm leaving that out of this fix since each residual is bounded and at most one extra plunge per rim crossing.

Also out of scope here: the V-crease being treated as a third opening (the depth-guard idea from the #1286 review) — that stays separate.
